Residual, non-decisive edge: enabled() takes the latest choices row by id (store.py:88-90), so a later 'objection'='off' row re-enables marketing. That is a withdrawal of the objection, not a bypass of an active objection, and is outside the stipulated facts.

Residual, non-decisive edge: cancellation on objection is scoped to cases owned by the objecting subject (store.py:98); a promotion job attached to a case whose owner differs from the objecting subject would not be cancelled, but the scenario's subject owns the queued campaign case, so this is not an in-scope counterexample.

The draft treats 'report' (insights) jobs as out of scope; that is correct for this rule, but note the objection-on branch does not cancel 'report' jobs (store.py:96-98), which is consistent with the rule's marketing-only scope.

anchors.explanation: preference() accepts purpose 'objection' with value 'on', persists a per-owner choices row, and on ('objection','on') cancels queued 'promotion' jobs for that owner's cases — the objection's effect on pending promotions.
enabled() reads the latest choices row per owner/purpose, so the persisted objection is consumed as a per-owner flag.

eligible_campaign() is the marketing selection predicate: requires promotions enabled and objection absent, evaluated per owner, so an objecting subject is excluded while other subscribers remain eligible.
campaign() queues 'promotion' jobs only for cases passing eligible_campaign(), gating future marketing selection on absence of objection.
drain() emits a promotion event only when eligible_campaign() holds at processing time; otherwise the job is left cancelled, so a queued promotion is not delivered after objection.
drain() skip logic applies only to restricted cases and non-'score' jobs; the 'score' service-decision branch is independent of marketing preferences, preserving necessary service processing.
Manual 'promotion' action also requires eligible_campaign(), so ad-hoc promotion queueing is likewise blocked by an objection.
Routing: /preference POST invokes store.preference with purpose/value; /campaign POST invokes store.campaign — the entrypoints connecting objection and marketing selection.
UI exposes the 'objection' preference toggle alongside promotions, surfacing the objection as a distinct per-owner control.

output.review_summary: Confirmed SUPPORTED. The objection path is wired end to end: /preference (app.py:85-86) calls store.preference, which persists an 'objection'=on choices row (store.py:92-95) and cancels queued 'promotion' jobs for that owner's cases (store.py:96-98). Marketing selection in eligible_campaign() requires promotions enabled and objection absent (store.py:100-103), gating campaign() queueing (store.py:105-109) and the manual promotion action (store.py:165-171), and is re-checked at drain time (store.py:140-143) so pending promotions are not delivered. Service 'score' jobs are independent of marketing preferences (store.py:126-135), and eligibility/cancellation are owner-scoped, leaving non-objecting subscribers eligible. Minor imprecision in the draft (drain leaves the job 'cancelled' rather than actively cancelling) does not change the outcome. No feasible in-scope counterexample found; assessment is static reading only, no execution performed.
